chunks: You have an excellent model in Abraham and those who were with him, when he said to his people: 'We are through with you, and those you worship other than God. We reject you. Enmity and hate have come between you and us for ever, unless you believe in God the One,' -- except for what he said to his father: 'I shall ask forgiveness for you, but I have no power to prevail with God for you.' 'O Lord, we place our trust in You, and turn to Him in penitence, and to You is our returning.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the primary role model for believers in Surah Al-Mumtahanah and what did they declare about idolatry?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse establishes the principle of *al-Bara'* (disassociation from polytheists) and *al-Wala'* (loyalty to God) as core tenets of faith, with the exception of Abraham's supplication for his father highlighting the balance between theological firmness and familial mercy. The phrase 'until you believe in Allah alone' is interpreted by scholars as indicating that the enmity is conditional upon the persistence of polytheism, serving as a timeless model for the community of the Ahl al-Bayt. This narrative reinforces the continuity of monotheistic identity from Abraham to the Prophet Muhammad and his progeny.
